analysis.title: Siemens AG (SIEGn.DE): Takeaways from management meeting following 4Q26
key_insights: After a CEO/CFO sell-side meeting in London, GS concludes Siemens has had a strong start to fiscal FY27 in automation, with double-digit software growth expected for the year.

Digital Industries (DI) automation orders: October saw strong spillover from September, setting up a very strong 1Q27, led by machine-building customers where Siemens sees some indirect AI capex benefit.

Management is limiting pre-buying and restocking risk in China to avoid a repeat of the post-COVID inventory overhang. It requires confirmation that distributor sell-through is complete before booking new orders.
Siemens is deploying locally designed and manufactured Chinese products in other markets to compete with Chinese peers, notably Inovance. It hopes this will not dilute margins.
FY27 software revenue is expected to grow at a double-digit rate, weighted toward 4Q27 because contract renewals fall in that quarter and 1Q27 starts from a lower base.
AI agents already contribute 5% of DI revenue and are growing faster than broader software. There is no token-cost liability because workloads run on client servers.
Data center backlog is about $7bn, with 70% scheduled for delivery in 2027 and the rest in 2028. Book-and-bill is healthy and exposure to neocloud customers is minimal.

Supplier constraints could somewhat limit near-term Smart Infrastructure (SI) growth upside despite vendor diversification. SI capex is expected to ramp capacity by about 30-50% in 2027 depending on the product, reaching full run-rate in 2028.

M&A: management has walked away from deals recently announced by peers because of elevated valuations. Pipeline screening has shifted toward building-services software, and management sees potential for $5-7bn hardware transactions. Priority verticals are data centers, life sciences and utilities.

Mobility: teams must target at least 60% platform conformity when bidding new orders to protect margins. Siemens divested bespoke light-rail operations, and metro production has moved to localized Indian manufacturing.
Mobility's fleet-data generation supports proprietary AI training, which puts the division at the center of Siemens' AI strategy.
GS rates Siemens Buy with a 12-month price target of €308 (price €281.70, upside 9.3%), valued 50% on SOTP and 50% on a sector-relative EV/IC to ROIC/WACC method.

market_movers.rationale: Strong FY27 automation start, double-digit software growth and about $7bn data center backlog. Price target €308 implies 9.3% upside from €281.70.

sector_views.rationale: GS is Buy on Siemens, citing automation recovery, software growth and data center visibility.

earnings_insights: GS estimates for Siemens (FY ends September): revenue €83,598.6mn FY26E, €95,146.9mn FY27E, €106,306.9mn FY28E, against €78,914.0mn reported in FY25.
GS EBIT estimates: €13,216.6mn FY26E, €15,536.3mn FY27E, €18,316.1mn FY28E, against €11,766.4mn in FY25.
GS EPS estimates: €11.85 FY26E, €13.93 FY27E, €16.66 FY28E, against €12.95 in FY25. Quarterly EPS: €3.14 reported for 6/26, then €3.03 9/26E, €3.14 12/26E, €3.30 3/27E.
GS P/E: 23.8x FY26E, 20.2x FY27E, 16.9x FY28E. EV/EBITDA (ex lease): 12.8x FY26E, 10.7x FY27E, 9.6x FY28E.
Software revenue is expected to show double-digit growth in FY27, weighted toward 4Q27 on contract renewal timing.
risk_factors: Prolonged automation weakness, especially in China.
China pre-buying and restocking could create an inventory overhang like the post-COVID one.
Supplier constraints could limit near-term SI growth upside, and data center orders could be volatile in the near term.
